mcq_fix.s: Which of the following statements regarding differentiated banking licences is correct? 1. The Nachiket Mor Committee was constituted in 2013. 2. Both Small Finance Banks and Payments Banks emerged from differentiated or niche banking licences. 3. Commercial banks are now licensed on an on-tap basis. Which of the statements given above are correct?
mcq_fix.why: Nachiket Mor Committee was set up in Sept 2013 but submitted its report in Jan 2014; reworded so key (all three) stays true

mcq_drop.why: dubious/obscure sweeping claim ('no banks in 19th-century Andhra')
oddly worded ('stated regulatory framework'); SFB on-tap minimum is now Rs 200 crore, so ambiguous
ambiguous: Bank of Calcutta (1806) was renamed Bank of Bengal, so options 3 and 4 both fit

notes_fix.why: 4th amalgamation phase merged 26 RRBs, cutting the count from 43 to 28
the 1788 Madras bank was the Carnatic Bank; Karnataka Bank Ltd dates from 1924 (Mangaluru)

patterns: APPSC asks direct dates/counts: 1969 and 1980 nationalisation, 19 July 1969, 14 banks; Lead Bank Scheme tied to bank nationalisation.
AP tilt: founder of Andhra Bank (Pattabhi Sitaramayya), SBI slogan/logo and bank-emblem items, ICICI-Videocon 'sweetheart' lending.

Other PSCs repeat: Oudh Commercial Bank 1881, first RRB 1975, SBI 1955, chronology RBI-SBI-LIC-1969, deposits are not bank assets, Service Area Approach under Lead Bank Scheme, NABARD as apex rural credit body.
App MCQs add SFB/payments-bank rules, RRB ownership and 2025-26 AP credit data that PYQs rarely touch; PYQs prefer one-line recall, logos and slogans.
